## Purpose and status

Build on PR173's forced dyadic band and pursue its universal marked-return descent criterion. **Full Collatz remains OPEN.** This continuation adds four Lean modules and **53 public theorems** to the earlier contraction packet, with exact source pins and separate execution and semantic-review evidence.

**Published head:** `65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695`  
**Tree:** `98984cbe1afdb8df056baa8fb583de19a71c5e19`

The PR remains stacked on PR173's branch. The imported forced-section sources are frozen at `fa0c9e2a2851e6324391e39c17afcb5913185aec`; the three unchanged phase/kernel vendor modules are frozen at PR178 head `0bb13b800e4e97f9fd3091b1a3d2e98b49911b7c`.

[Scientific entry point](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/README.md) · [Executed proof checks](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/reports/2026-11-21-dyadic-descent/continuation/README.md)

## New kernel-checked results

### 1. Power-saving marked returns on long exponent blocks

There are arbitrarily large q such that, with H=floor(q/10), every supplied odd-offset certificate T^h(r)=1 with h<=H works simultaneously for every exponent

```
2q+H+1 <= d <= 12q-H.
```

For n=2^d+r, the proof gives an actual positive marked-return index k and endpoint y=R^k(n) satisfying

```
y < n,    y^120 < n^119,    Basin(n) iff Basin(y).
```

The short certificate supplies r<=2^h; no separate fixed offset-size budget is assumed. An exponential coefficient budget yields the fixed source-scale power saving.

For r=1, whole blocks 2q+1<=d<=12q work. The exact finite counting result gives arbitrarily large cutoffs M with at least 5M/6 successful positive exponents. This is an **upper-density statement about exponents**, not all starting values, and not a bound at every cutoff.

The two coverage gaps remain: these selected blocks need not cover every prescribed exponent, and their short-certificate budget does not cover arbitrary band offsets. In fact the growing-budget range still implies r^21<n.

[ExponentCoverage.lean](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/ExponentCoverage.lean) · [Complete statement and proof](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/EXPONENT_COVERAGE.md)

### 2. Uniform finite temporal bounds on one actual odd orbit

For a prefix of N distinct odd states x_j, the proof gives

```
sum_{j<N} 1/x_j <= H_N <= 1+log N.
```

This controls the exact height/valuation cocycle and gives a finite Fourier error O_a(log N/N) at each positive integer frequency a, with no assumed escape rate. The finite nonnegative kernel then yields

```
(floor(log_2 N)+1) * V_n(N) <= 196608*N,
```

where V_n(N) counts marked states among the first N odd states. Only those N states must be distinct; the endpoint at N may repeat. An all-horizon version retains global injectivity, and another obtains it from actual unboundedness.

The constant is explicit and conservative. Sparse temporal occupation does not erase the positive mass of a fixed surviving source and is not a spatial survivor-count estimate.

[AnalyticCoupling.lean](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/AnalyticCoupling.lean) · [TemporalDensity.lean](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/TemporalDensity.lean) · [Quantitative proof](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/TEMPORAL_DENSITY.md)

### 3. Four possible initial valuations for an original no-descent source

Exact ordinary forward identities show that any n>1 with T^t(n)>=n for every t must satisfy

```
v_2(9n+1) in {2,3,5,7}.
```

This applies to a least nonconvergent source and a minimum of a nontrivial cycle. It does not restrict every later state above the original floor. The odd-gap smaller partner is itself an earlier forward iterate.

This is a finite-prefix sieve: every valuation at least eight already descends by clock eight. The four classes form a necessary cover, not the exact set of eight-step survivors; 39 belongs to the cover but reaches 38 at clock eight. No complete selector on the remaining unbounded classes is claimed.

[MergerDispatch.lean](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/MergerDispatch.lean) · [Ordinary-source interpretation](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/research/lean-dyadic-descent-20261121/MERGER_DISPATCH.md)

### 4. Exact first-band offset obstruction

Kernel `decide` checks n=2^601-1. Its first marked shortcut iterate is

```
T^7(n) = 3^7*2^594-1 = 2^605 + (139*2^594-1).
```

The canonical offset exceeds the original source by 11*2^594. The same proof checks all seven earlier failures of markedness and oddness through clock seven. Thus first-band entry does not justify induction on an offset merely because it is smaller than the later marked value. This is not a counterexample to convergence.

## Actual validation

- Lean **4.34.1**, commit `5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52`; tracked-clean Mathlib `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`.
- Fresh final replay compiled all **seven continuation/vendor modules** and the combined **53-theorem audit**, using `-j1 -DwarningAsError=true`.
- Seven unchanged baseline modules were reused from a successful fresh build earlier in this session. The final receipt embeds that actual seven-command receipt and verifies source/compiler pins and artifact hashes; it does not describe all units as a single fresh run.
- Every audited dependency closure contains only a subset of **propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound**. No sorry, native_decide, or custom convergence axiom supplies a result.
- All fourteen Lean source hashes matched before and after compilation and again at publication. The three vendor Git blob IDs were compared with the frozen GitHub source bytes.
- Separate internal agents checked the mathematics and quantifier interpretation of all four new modules. The reviews distinguish selected-scale coverage, original-source floors, finite-prefix injectivity, and spatial versus temporal counts.
- All **five required repository checks** passed in a complete clean checkout of the local proof commit, and passed again at the **actual published head above**, with **361 tracked files** and an unchanged checkout. These are integrity checks, separate from Lean proof checking.

[Full Lean receipt](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/reports/2026-11-21-dyadic-descent/continuation/LEAN_RECEIPT.json) · [All axiom audits](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/reports/2026-11-21-dyadic-descent/continuation/AXIOM_AUDIT.json) · [Semantic reviews](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/reports/2026-11-21-dyadic-descent/continuation/SEMANTIC_REVIEW.md) · [Source binding](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/reports/2026-11-21-dyadic-descent/continuation/SOURCE_BINDING.json)

## Prior results and exact remaining step

The previous arbitrarily strong marked-return contraction theorem, fixed-offset lifts, phase-frequency results, and their original receipts are retained unchanged. The [previous PR description](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/65ee193029bc04f5ee1b9ca25b6b96d6f1055695/reports/2026-11-21-dyadic-descent/continuation/PR182_BEFORE.json) preserves its exact historical evidence.

A full proof still requires universal eventual descent on the marked section, a complete smaller-source common-future selection, or a fixed-source transport estimate strong enough to force absorption. The new estimates and families do not discharge that universal step.
